2607.12520.title: The Model Knows Your Project, Not You: Measuring Recognition in LLMs with NameRank
2607.12520.paper_summary: What a frontier model recalls about a person or tool from its own weights -- before any retrieval step -- often shapes the first description a human sees, making that parametric corpus presence a measurement problem. Citations explain about a third of whether a model recognizes a researcher; we target the residual and build NameRank, a [0,1] recognition score: each of 4,685 entities in 54 cohorts is probed with one open-ended question across 36 models, and an independent judge returns a binary verdict against a curated gold -- did the model state a specific, non-guessable fact about this exact entity? -- so hallucination, context echo, and guesses earn nothing. Synthetic-null entities hold the floor near zero, and verdicts track the entity, not the model. One thesis organizes the findings: recognition is paid to named, indexable artifacts, not to credentials or titles. Every Olympic-style credential sits below a working-researcher baseline, because no named artifact ships with the medal, yet the ranking inverts at the marquee tier, where Nobel, Turing, and Fields laureates saturate the panel. For independent creators the tool out-ranks its maker, and the credential that does propagate is a named method or awarded paper. Being one of many named contributors to a celebrated artifact, by contrast, earns almost nothing -- the authors listed on a flagship model report or system card sit near the recognition floor -- because recognition attaches to the artifact's own distinctive name, not to the roster behind it. No bibliometric predicts recognition well; top-density institutions out-recognize peers at matched citations; and on 258 news events recognition loads on peak salience, not persistence. A self-report probe shows introspection reads a corpus prior, not its own knowledge.
2607.12520.paper_summary_zh: 一個前沿模型對於其自身權重所回憶起的某個人或工具——在任何檢索步驟之前——往往塑造了人類所見的第一個描述，使得該參數化語料庫的存在成為一個測量問題。引用解釋了約三分之一的模型是否能識別研究者；我們針對剩餘部分並建立了 NameRank，一個 [0,1] 的識別分數：在 54 個隊列中的 4,685 個實體中，每個實體都通過 36 個模型進行了一個開放式問題的探測，而一位獨立評審則根據經過策劃的黃金標準給出二元判決——模型是否陳述了關於這個具體實體的一個特定、不可猜測的事實？——因此，幻覺、上下文回聲和猜測都不會得分。合成空實體的得分接近零，判決追蹤的是實體，而不是模型。一個論文組織了這些發現：識別是針對命名的、可索引的文物，而不是證書或頭銜。每一個奧林匹克風格的證書都低於工作研究者的基準，因為沒有命名的文物隨著獎牌發放，但在標誌性層級的排名卻顛倒，諾貝爾、圖靈和菲爾茲獎得主充斥著評審小組。對於獨立創作者，工具的排名高於其創作者，而能夠傳播的證書是命名的方法或獲獎的論文。相比之下，作為一個受人尊敬的文物的眾多命名貢獻者之一幾乎不會獲得任何認可——在一個旗艦模型報告或系統卡上列出的作者接近識別底線——因為認可附著於文物自身獨特的名稱，而不是其背後的名單。沒有任何文獻計量學能很好地預測識別；頂尖密度的機構在匹配引用中超越同儕；而在 258 個新聞事件中，識別加載在高峰顯著性上，而不是持久性上。一個自我報告的探測顯示，內省讀取的是先前的語料庫，而不是自身的知識。
2607.12520.author: Bojie Li et.al.
